port-moresby-1: Port Moresby wildlife park with tree kangaroos, cassowaries, birds of paradise and a walk-through WWII aviary.
port-moresby-2: Waigani museum of over 30,000 objects, from traditional boats to Sepik art, with WWII planes and tanks outside.
port-moresby-4: Commonwealth war cemetery 19 km north-east of Port Moresby, with 3,824 graves, many from the Kokoda campaign.
port-moresby-5: Waigani's Parliament House, styled on a Maprik haus tambaran spirit house, with group tours on weekdays.
port-moresby-6: Gordon's largest produce market in Port Moresby, selling vegetables from other provinces; go with a known driver.
port-moresby-7: Private resort island in Bootless Bay with snorkelling and diving; day visits by ferry from Tahira, booked ahead.
mount-wilhelm: PNG's highest mountain at 4,509 m, climbed with a local guide from Keglsugl, with a night on the mountain.
mount-giluwe: Extinct volcano in the Southern Highlands, second-highest in PNG, climbed with a guide in about a day.
lake-kutubu: Ramsar-listed upland lake south-west of Mendi, home to ten fish found nowhere else, with villages reached by canoe.
lihir-group: Gold-mining island group off New Ireland, reached by daily flight from Port Moresby, with Kunaye Beach Resort.
manus-island: Largest of the Admiralty Islands, with Lorengau on Seeadler Harbor, WWII relics and reefs for diving; reached by air.
buka-island: Island where flights arrive for Bougainville, with Buka Passage boat trips and a road circling the island.
sohano-island: Island 10 minutes by boat from Buka Market, with a mona canoe, an ANZAC memorial and views across the passage.
mount-balbi: Active volcano and Bougainville's highest peak at 2,715 m, climbed over three days from Wakunai with a local guide.
nissan-island: Crescent island around a turquoise lagoon, with WWII airstrip relics; a four-hour boat ride from Buka.
alotau-1: Former colonial port island at the entrance to Milne Bay, 20 minutes to walk round, reached by boat from Alotau.
alotau-2: Rainforest headland with a fringing reef and dive resort, reached by sea, with over 60 dive sites within an hour.
alotau-3: Mountainous D'Entrecasteaux island of rainforest trails and birdwatching, reached by boat from Alotau.
alotau-5: Largest of the D'Entrecasteaux Islands, a geothermal rainforest island with birdwatching, reached only by boat.
trobriand-islands: Raised coral atolls with white beaches and preserved traditional dancing, reached by twice-weekly flight.
louisiade-archipelago: About 100 islands ringed by coral reefs, known for diving and visited mainly by yacht; ask before fishing.
misima-island: Most accessible Louisiade island, with quiet beaches and a gold mine closed in 2004; reached by air from Alotau.
goodenough-island: Volcanic D'Entrecasteaux island rising to Mount Vineuo, with rainforest and birdwatching; reached from Alotau.
madang-1: Working harbour lighthouse in Madang, also the memorial to WWII coastwatchers who reported Japanese movements.
madang-2: Busy central market in Madang where people bring Highlands produce to sell, mostly fruit and vegetables.
madang-3: Road-free island a five-minute boat ride from Madang, with two villages, gardens and a lagoon beach.
karkar-island: Oval volcanic island in the Bismarck Sea with an active twin-caldera volcano and a mountain view down to Madang.
lae-war-cemetery: Commonwealth WWII cemetery beside Lae Botanic Gardens, begun in 1944 and holding the Lae Memorial to the missing.
lae-rainforest-habitat: Walk-through rainforest aviary with birds of paradise at Unitech in Lae; reported run-down, so check before going.
bulolo-gold-dredges: Gold dredges left in the Bulolo jungle, every part airlifted in by Junkers aircraft before dredging ended in 1965.
rabaul-1: Active volcano above Rabaul reached by road, with hot springs and ash deposits; climbs start here with a guide.
rabaul-3: Volcano observatory on Mount Tavanabatir with a lookout over Rabaul town, the bay and the volcano.
rabaul-4: WWII tunnel near Mount Vulcan with Japanese barges still inside, down a rough unmarked track at Karavia.
rabaul-5: 1937 New Guinea Club building turned museum of Rabaul's history, with many photographs, opposite Yamamoto's bunker.
rabaul-6: Commonwealth war cemetery near Kokopo for WWII servicemen from many countries, with a Japanese war memorial.
rabaul-7: Museum in central Kokopo of Japanese war relics, with a few photographs, opposite the waterfront golf course.
rabaul-8: Group of 13 islands about 45 minutes by boat from Kokopo, visited for diving, snorkelling and picnics.
kimbe-bay: Bay off Kimbe with over 900 fish and 400 coral species, reached by dive boat from Kimbe or Walindi.
kokoda-track-1: Southern trailhead of the 96 km Kokoda Track, 50 km from Port Moresby; treks need a licensed operator and permit.
kokoda-track-2: Site of the 1942 Battle of Isurava on the Kokoda Track, with a memorial and museum reached only on foot.
buna: Coastal Oro Province village with WWII relics and a memorial plaque to the 32nd Red Arrow Division at its entrance.
gona: Coastal village in Oro Province where Japanese forces landed in 1942; visited for WWII relics, with a local guide.
maprik: Sepik town whose district is known for forward-leaning haus tambaran spirit houses; ask permission before entering.
sepik-river: River reached from Wewak by motor-canoe, with day trips, overnight expeditions and village stays.
kairiru-island: Island 30 minutes by boat from Wewak with waterfalls, snorkelling and natural hot springs.
mushu-island: Small island reached by boat from Wewak, one of four within an hour of town.
cape-wom: Peace park near Wewak where General Adachi signed the Japanese surrender in 1945, with some tunnels still open.
lake-murray: Remote lake and wetland in Western Province for birdwatching and fishing, reached by light aircraft then boat.
tonda-wildlife-management-area: Ramsar wetland of 590,000 hectares on the Indonesian border, reached by charter flight to Bensbach Wildlife Lodge.
kerema: Gulf Province's capital on the Gulf of Papua coast, a basic base with a few hotels, reached by road or air.
kikori: Small fishing town on the Kikori River delta, used as a base for birdwatching in the delta.
goroka: Eastern Highlands capital and the region's main hub, the base for the Goroka Show, Asaro Mudmen and Mount Michael.
mount-hagen: Western Highlands capital and air hub, the base for visits to Kuk, Baiyer River and the town's market.
kainantu: Market town on the Highlands Highway between Lae and Goroka, with a cultural centre and local pottery.
mendi: Southern Highlands capital and gateway to Lake Kutubu and Mount Giluwe, with a Friday and Saturday market.
kundiawa: Simbu Province capital and the departure point for the Mount Wilhelm climb, reached via Keglsugl.
kavieng: New Ireland's capital at the island's northern tip, a gateway for diving, surfing, fishing and boat trips, with wartime history.
lorengau: Manus Province capital beside Seeadler Harbour, with a market, garamut dance tradition and sago village visits.
buka: Bougainville's busiest town, with a market, boats across Buka Passage and waterfront restaurants.
lae: Papua New Guinea's second city and Morobe's capital, where the Highlands Highway starts, with a botanic garden.
wau: Gold-rush town at about 1,100 m, the inland end of the Black Cat Track, with the Wau Ecology Institute nearby.
bulolo: Former gold-dredging town on the Bulolo River, 32 km north-west of Wau, with dredge relics and a golf course.
rabaul-2: East New Britain's current provincial capital and airport gateway, with markets and a war museum.
kokoda-track-3: Station town at the northern end of the Kokoda Track, with the only airfield on the track and the finish of most walks.
popondetta: Oro Province capital and gateway, with flights from Port Moresby and the road to Kokoda; a base rather than a sight.
tufi: Fishing and dive town on the Cape Nelson peninsula, the base for the Tufi fjords, reef dives and tapa-cloth making.
wewak: East Sepik's capital and the gateway for Sepik River trips, with a wartime Japanese airbase and surrender site.
vanimo: Sandaun Province capital on the Indonesian border, the base for nearby surf breaks and coastal headlands.
vanimo-surf-breaks: Reef and point breaks west of Vanimo with waves up to 3 m, best September to March and for experienced surfers only.
daru: Western Province's capital on Daru Island at the Fly River mouth, the domestic air gateway to the province, mainly for fishing.
kiunga: River port on the Fly River at the southern end of the Kiunga-Tabubil Highway, a base for birdwatching and nature tours.
port-moresby-3: Port Moresby's main public beach, a kilometre of white sand with a boardwalk, courts and an amphitheatre, good for a walk.
tari: Capital of Hela Province and the base for visits to Huli villages and birdwatching around the Tari Basin.
kimbe: West New Britain's capital and palm-oil port on Kimbe Bay, and the gateway and base for the bay's diving.
